title: Myasthenia gravis and junctional disorders

steps.tx: **Myasthenia gravis** is an autoimmune postsynaptic neuromuscular junction disorder caused by antibodies to **acetylcholine receptors** (AChR-Ab, present in **85%** of generalized cases), muscle-specific kinase (MuSK), or LRP4. Antibody binding produces complement-mediated destruction of post-synaptic junctional folds and depletion of functional receptors.

Antibody binding produces complement-mediated destruction of post-synaptic junctional folds and depletion of functional receptors.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating post-synaptic acetylcholine receptor blockade and fatigable weakness in myasthenia gravis.
vis.caption: Post-synaptic acetylcholine receptor blockade in myasthenia gravis (StewardMD).

steps.tx: The clinical hallmark of myasthenia gravis is fluctuating, painless **muscle weakness** that worsens with repetitive activity and improves with rest, most commonly presenting with **ptosis** and diplopia. Asymmetric eyelid droop and variable ocular misalignment worsen toward the end of the day or during prolonged upward gaze.

left.title: Ocular Manifestations
points: Cogan twitch sign on saccadic refixation
Enhanced ptosis test on manual eyelid lift

right.title: Bulbar & Systemic Signs
points: Nasal voice and dysarthria with speech fatigue
Dysphagia and chewing fatigue on firm foods
Proximal limb weakness with preserved reflexes

steps.tx: **Single-fiber electromyography** demonstrating increased **jitter** and impulse blocking is the most sensitive diagnostic electrophysiological test for myasthenia gravis, displaying greater than **95%** sensitivity. Variable neuromuscular transmission time between two muscle fibers of the same motor unit demonstrates defective junctional safety factors.

Variable neuromuscular transmission time between two muscle fibers of the same motor unit demonstrates defective junctional safety factors.

left.title: Diagnostic Sensitivity
points: Most sensitive test when serology is negative

right.title: Technical Parameters
points: Evaluates extensor digitorum communis or frontalis
Pathological impulse blocking with severe jitter

steps.tx: Chest CT or MRI is mandatory in all newly diagnosed myasthenia gravis patients to identify **thymoma**, present in **10%** to **15%** of patients, or **thymic** follicular hyperplasia present in up to 70% of early-onset cases. Thymoma resection is necessary to prevent local mediastinal invasion and malignant pleural dissemination.

rows: Young females with early-onset generalized disease
Late-onset disease or anti-MuSK positive cohorts
Thymectomy generally not indicated in anti-MuSK

steps.tx: **Thymectomy** improves clinical outcomes and reduces corticosteroid requirements in AChR-antibody-positive generalized myasthenia gravis patients aged **18** to **65** without thymoma according to the **MGTX** trial. Operative intervention removes the primary site of autoantigen sensitization and pathological germinal center development in mediastinal tissues.

Operative intervention removes the primary site of autoantigen sensitization and pathological germinal center development in mediastinal tissues.

left.title: MGTX Trial Verification
points: Randomized surgical vs medical therapy alone
Statistically lower Quantitative Myasthenia Gravis scores
Significant reduction in ongoing corticosteroid requirements

steps.tx: **Myasthenic crisis** with respiratory failure is managed in an intensive care setting with urgent plasma exchange or IVIG while temporarily discontinuing **cholinesterase inhibitors** to avoid excess airway secretions and clarify cholinergic versus myasthenic weakness during sudden acute ventilatory decompensation clinical episodes.
steps.say: Myasthenic crisis with respiratory failure is managed in an intensive care setting with urgent plasma exchange or IVIG while temporarily discontinuing cholinesterase inhibitors to avoid excess airway secretions and clarify cholinergic versus myasthenic weakness during acute ventilatory decompensation.

left.title: Acute Crisis Resuscitation
points: Elective intubation for vital capacity <15 mL/kg
Negative inspiratory force weaker than -20 cmH2O
Urgent plasma exchange (5 sessions) or IVIG (2 g/kg)

steps.tx: **Lambert-Eaton** myasthenic syndrome is a presynaptic disorder targeting voltage-gated P/Q-type **calcium channels**, strongly linked to small cell lung cancer, characterized by hyporeflexia, dry mouth, and paradoxical post-exercise facilitation where strength temporarily improves across repeatedly tested proximal muscle groups in neuromuscular clinics.
steps.say: Lambert-Eaton myasthenic syndrome is a presynaptic disorder targeting voltage-gated P/Q-type calcium channels strongly linked to small cell lung cancer characterized by hyporeflexia dry mouth and paradoxical post-exercise facilitation where strength temporarily improves across tested muscle groups.

vis.alt: Diagram illustrating presynaptic voltage-gated calcium channels versus postsynaptic acetylcholine receptors.
vis.caption: Presynaptic calcium channel autoimmunity in Lambert-Eaton syndrome (StewardMD).

steps.tx: **Repetitive nerve stimulation** in LEMS demonstrates low baseline CMAP amplitude that displays dramatic **increment** exceeding **100%** following high-frequency **20** to **50** Hz stimulation or **10** seconds of maximal isometric exercise, confirming presynaptic calcium channel dysfunction in specialized clinical electrophysiology testing evaluations.

left.title: LEMS Electrophysiology
points: Markedly reduced baseline CMAP amplitude (<2 mV)
Rapid intracellular calcium accumulation in terminals

right.title: Therapeutic Strategy
points: Underlying small cell lung cancer oncological therapy
